narrativeReportMd:
# SampledData R4-to-R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
`SampledData` has hard R4-to-R6 instance breaks. The R4 mandatory `period` element is no longer present; R6 introduces a different timing model using `interval` plus mandatory `intervalUnit`, or irregular `offsets`, with a new invariant requiring exactly one timing representation. R6 also widens `data` to allow arbitrary coded tokens via an optional `codeMap`, creating substantial R6-to-R4 round-trip risk and parser/runtime risk.

## Scope
The analysis is scoped to the local core datatype StructureDefinitions and directly relevant local UCUM ValueSet files. Inherited base datatype and Element changes are excluded and called out in `scope.outOfScope`.

## Main migration themes
The main migration concern is timing. R4 instances carry `period` as milliseconds; R6 instances must use `interval` with an explicit UCUM `intervalUnit`, or use `offsets` for irregular sampling. A simple R4-to-R6 transform can usually map `period` to `interval` and add `intervalUnit` = `ms`, but raw R4 JSON will not validate as R6. R6-to-R4 conversion can be lossy when units are not milliseconds or when irregular offsets are used. The second theme is data token semantics: R6 can carry non-numeric codes in `data` and identify their meaning with `codeMap`, which R4 cannot represent in the base datatype.

## Highest-impact findings
High-impact findings are `SampledData.period` replacement, required `SampledData.intervalUnit`, irregular `SampledData.offsets`, and coded `data`/`codeMap`. These affect validation, generated model APIs, conversion, and waveform/data interpretation.

## Findings requiring human review
Human review is most useful for the coded-data semantics and the new `sdd-1` timing invariant. The computable definitions are clear, but the supplied inputs do not include an official diff, change rationale, full rendered narrative page, or concrete ConceptMaps.

## Backward-compatible design observations
Some goals could have been achieved less disruptively by keeping a deprecated `period` alias or defaulting omitted units to milliseconds. That would have reduced raw instance and codegen breaks but would also preserve ambiguous timing semantics and make the R6 model less explicit.

## Follow-up analysis
Separate reports should cover the `DataType` base shift, inherited `Element`/`Extension` behavior, UCUM terminology handling, and ConceptMap/cross-version conversion strategy for coded sampled data.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: `SampledData` has hard breaking changes: R4 `period` is removed/replaced, R6 requires a new UCUM `intervalUnit`, and R6 adds irregular offsets plus coded data semantics that are not cleanly representable in R4. The highest uncertainty is not whether the computable changes exist, but the intended migration policy and exact coded-token semantics.
summary.migrationThemesMd: R4-to-R6 migration should transform `period` milliseconds to `interval` plus `intervalUnit` = `ms`, then validate the `sdd-1` exactly-one timing rule. R6-to-R4 migration must detect `offsets`, non-millisecond or non-time interval units, and coded `data` tokens with `codeMap`; these may require extensions, lossy approximation, or rejection. Generated code and validators must be updated for removed/added properties and the new required binding.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for the structural and validation findings because they are directly visible in both StructureDefinitions and confirmed by package index entries. Confidence is medium for migration intent and real-world prevalence because no official diff, ballot rationale, full narrative page, terminology expansion, or concrete ConceptMap instances were supplied.

findings.title: R4 `period` was removed and replaced by R6 `interval` timing semantics

oldState.summary: R4 had mandatory `period` as the time between samples in milliseconds.

semanticText.definition: The length of time between sampling times, measured in milliseconds.
semanticText.comment: This is usually a whole number.

oldState.narrativeMd: Every valid R4 `SampledData` instance had to include `period`, and its unit was fixed by definition to milliseconds.

newState.summary: R6 has `interval` as one timing alternative; it is 0..1 in raw cardinality but constrained by `sdd-1` to be present when `offsets` is absent.

constraints.human: A SampledData SHALL have either an interval and offsets but not both

semanticText.definition: Amount of intervalUnits between samples, e.g. milliseconds for time-based sampling.
semanticText.comment: This is usually a whole number.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 no longer defines `period`; the equivalent regular-sampling representation is `interval`, interpreted through the separate required `intervalUnit` element.

facts.note: The R4 element is absent from the R6 local element set.
The R6 element has the same decimal type and same RIM mapping to GLIST.increment but generalized unit semantics.
The apparent decrease is coupled to the new mutually exclusive `offsets` alternative.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: `period` and `interval` are matched because both are decimal regular-sampling increments, both map to `GLIST.increment`, and the R6 definition explicitly describes milliseconds as an example of `intervalUnits`.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is a direct serialization and validation break. An R4 instance containing `period` uses an element name that is not defined in R6, and without a transform it will also lack the R6 `interval` or `offsets` timing representation. Generated R4 classes and client code that expose `.period` must be updated to `.interval` plus unit handling. R6-to-R4 conversion is only straightforward when the R6 regular interval can be expressed as milliseconds.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Wrong sample timing can change interpretation of waveform or high-frequency device data. The risk is usually migration/business correctness rather than direct validation only.

justification.inferredGoal: Generalize regular sample spacing from fixed milliseconds to an explicitly unit-coded interval and align it with the new offsets alternative.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain `period` as the regular-sampling interval field, clarify that it is measured in `intervalUnit`, and allow missing units to mean milliseconds for legacy R4 content.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 goal of generalizing regular sample spacing beyond implicit milliseconds is reasonable, but the element-identity break from `period` to `interval` was not clearly necessary. The primary definitions show that both elements are decimal regular-sampling increments; R6 could have broadened and clarified the existing `period` element instead of renaming it. The remaining tradeoff is mostly clarity and model tidiness rather than a need to reject the R4 element name.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base R6 design could keep `SampledData.period` for regular sampling, update its definition from fixed milliseconds to an amount expressed in `intervalUnit`, and treat omitted `intervalUnit` as `ms` for R4-compatible content. `offsets` could remain the irregular-sampling alternative. This would preserve old serialized instances far better than a rename. The cost is living with the older name and a compatibility default, but it avoids duplicate `period`/`interval` fields if R6 simply retains the old field rather than adding an alias.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: This preserves R4 instances and avoids a same-fact rename, but it keeps the older `period` name and a legacy implicit-millisecond path.

evidence.detail: R4 defines `period` as 1..1 decimal with short text `Number of milliseconds between samples`.
evidence.quote: The length of time between sampling times, measured in milliseconds.

evidence.detail: R6 defines `interval` as 0..1 decimal with condition `sdd-1`.
evidence.quote: Amount of intervalUnits between samples, e.g. milliseconds for time-based sampling.

evidence.detail: R6 adds `sdd-1`, making `interval` part of an exactly-one choice with `offsets`.

examples.examplesMd: The example is a datatype fragment. It illustrates the regular millisecond migration pattern: rename `period` to `interval` and add `intervalUnit` = `ms`.

findings.narrativeMd: `SampledData.period` is not present in R6. Its closest successor is `SampledData.interval`, but the semantic unit moved out of the element definition and into `intervalUnit`. This affects raw JSON/XML compatibility and generated APIs: old instances and code that use `period` will fail against R6 unless they are transformed.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4-valid SampledData fragment with `period` is not R6-valid as-is because `period` is an unknown element in R6 and the R6 timing representation is not satisfied. R6 regular intervals can often be mapped back to R4 by converting to milliseconds, but that mapping can be lossy or invalid for units that do not have a safe millisecond conversion.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: For R4-to-R6, map `period` to `interval` and set `intervalUnit` to the UCUM code `ms`; do not also populate `offsets`. Update generated classes, serializers, validators, and FHIRPath expressions from `period` to `interval`. For R6-to-R4, only map `interval` to `period` when the unit can be converted to milliseconds and the conversion policy is explicit.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The change probably reflects a real modeling improvement, but it was not fully backward compatible. A deprecated `period` alias or an optional default of milliseconds could have reduced breakage, at the cost of duplicate representations and less explicit units.

freshReview.narrativeMd: `SampledData.period` is a required R4 timing element and R6 no longer defines that path, replacing the regular-sampling concept with `interval` plus a separate unit. An R4 Observation carrying `valueSampledData.period` is therefore not accepted as the same path in R6, and generated/client code that reads or writes `.period` must be changed. The rename looks broader than necessary for the R6 goal because the regular-spacing decimal could have stayed on the old wire name with clarified semantics, so this deserves renewed design review even though SampledData was trial-use in R4.
keyEvidence: R4 `SampledData.period` is 1..1 decimal and defined as milliseconds between samples.
R6 has no `SampledData.period`; R6 `SampledData.interval` is 0..1 decimal and participates in `sdd-1`.
R6 `SampledData.intervalUnit` is 1..1 with a required UCUM binding, showing that units were separated from the interval amount.
Observation.value[x] and Observation.component.value[x] include SampledData in both R4 and R6.
R4 StructureDefinition and r4-maturity metadata checked: SampledData standards status is trial-use.
freshReview.fmmEffect: R4 SampledData is trial-use rather than normative, so stability expectations are softer; however this is the required timing path for every R4 SampledData and is exposed through Observation value paths, so trial-use status does not make the same-fact rename harmless.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: raw R4 instances use `period`, which is not an R6 element; runtime/API/codegen also changes because the `.period` property is replaced by the R6 timing model.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A less-breaking base design appears plausible: keep `period` as the regular-sampling amount, broaden its definition to use `intervalUnit`, and use `offsets` only for irregular sampling. The tradeoff is carrying a legacy time-flavored name and possibly an implicit millisecond default, but it avoids rejecting the old wire path.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree with the existing High impact and Yes alternative judgment; the fresh assessment independently finds a direct path break and a plausible lower-cost base design.

findings.title: R6 adds mandatory `intervalUnit` with required UCUM binding

oldState.summary: R4 had no interval-unit element; `period` was implicitly measured in milliseconds.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 did not require any unit code for sample spacing because the unit was built into the `period` definition.

newState.summary: R6 requires `intervalUnit` 1..1 as a code bound required to all UCUM units.

binding.description: Units of measure allowed for an element.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: The local ValueSet compose includes all UCUM codes from `http://unitsofmeasure.org`; no live expansion or external UCUM version comparison was performed.

semanticText.short: The measurement unit of the interval between samples
semanticText.definition: The measurement unit in which the sample interval is expressed.

newState.narrativeMd: Every R6 `SampledData` must carry an explicit UCUM unit for the interval or offsets.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: `intervalUnit` has no R4 element counterpart; the old state was an implicit milliseconds convention on `period`.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is a hard R4-to-R6 validation break because no valid R4 instance can contain the new required `intervalUnit` field in the base datatype. Validators will reject R6 instances without it. Runtime code that constructs SampledData must now supply a UCUM code and handle terminology validation. R6-to-R4 conversion loses explicit unit information unless it can be converted back to milliseconds.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Unit errors in high-frequency sample data can materially alter interpretation of measurement timing or spacing.

justification.inferredGoal: Make sample spacing units explicit and allow units beyond milliseconds.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Make `intervalUnit` optional or default it to `ms` for legacy regular-sampling content while requiring it for new non-millisecond or offsets use.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Requiring a UCUM unit is a reasonable safety and interoperability goal because R4 encoded milliseconds only in prose. The raw-instance break is real, but an optional/defaulted unit would only partially meet the R6 goal: implementations would still need to infer units when the field is absent, which is exactly the ambiguity R6 appears to be correcting.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best less-breaking base design would allow `intervalUnit` to be absent for migrated R4 regular samples and define that absence as `ms`, possibly while requiring `intervalUnit` whenever offsets or non-millisecond intervals are used. That preserves old data but makes validators and receivers support both explicit and implicit unit semantics. Because unit mistakes can change sampled-data interpretation, that tradeoff is material rather than a low-cost compatibility tweak.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: This would preserve more R4 content, but it materially weakens R6's explicit-unit guarantee and perpetuates the hidden millisecond assumption.

evidence.detail: R4 `period` uses milliseconds in the definition and there is no `SampledData.intervalUnit` element.
R6 defines `intervalUnit` as 1..1 code with a required UCUM binding.
evidence.quote: The measurement unit in which the sample interval is expressed.

evidence.detail: The R6 UCUM value set includes all codes from `http://unitsofmeasure.org`.

examples.examplesMd: The R4 fragment lacks any unit field because R4 fixed `period` to milliseconds. The migrated R6 fragment makes that unit explicit.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 adds `SampledData.intervalUnit` as mandatory metadata for sample spacing. This is not just a new optional annotation; it is a required element with a required UCUM binding, so migrated content must choose a valid UCUM code.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Raw R4 SampledData cannot satisfy R6 validation because `intervalUnit` was not present in R4. Conversely, R6 content using explicit units may not be representable in R4 without converting to milliseconds and losing the original unit expression.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: For R4-to-R6, populate `intervalUnit` with `ms` when converting `period`. Validate the code against UCUM and add tests for missing, invalid, and non-time unit values. For R6-to-R4, define whether units are converted to milliseconds, preserved in an extension, or rejected if not safely convertible.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The mandatory field is probably justified by the need to eliminate implicit units. A less-breaking optional default could have helped old instances but would provide weaker conformance guarantees and make unit mistakes harder to detect.

freshReview.narrativeMd: `SampledData.intervalUnit` is a new mandatory code with a required UCUM binding. Any base R4 SampledData lacks this element, so a raw migrated instance cannot be R6-valid, and constructors/validators must now supply and validate a UCUM unit. This is a real hard break, but the R6 goal is strong: sample spacing and offset units should be computable instead of embedded only in `period` prose. Making the unit optional or defaulted to milliseconds would preserve more old content, but it would keep an implicit-unit mode that R6 is reasonably trying to remove.
keyEvidence: R4 has `SampledData.period` in milliseconds and no `SampledData.intervalUnit` element.
R6 `SampledData.intervalUnit` is 1..1 code with required binding to `http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/ucum-units|6.0.0-ballot4`.
R6 `SampledData.interval` and `SampledData.offsets` both depend on the unit context for correct interpretation.
R4 metadata checked: SampledData is trial-use.
freshReview.fmmEffect: Trial-use status softens the stability objection compared with normative content. Because unit errors can change interpretation of sampled measurements, the mandatory explicit unit still carries a reasonable safety and interoperability justification.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4-valid SampledData cannot contain `intervalUnit`, while R6 requires it; runtime/API/codegen is also affected because producers must populate a new required property and terminology validators must check UCUM.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A partial less-breaking design exists: make `intervalUnit` 0..1 and define absence as milliseconds, perhaps while requiring it for offsets or non-millisecond intervals. That would preserve legacy content but materially weakens the explicit-unit guarantee and forces receivers to support implicit units indefinitely.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree with the existing High impact and Partial alternative judgment; the break is hard, but the fresh judgment treats the required unit as proportionate to the R6 goal.

findings.title: R6 `offsets` supports irregular sampling that R4 cannot represent

oldState.summary: R4 had only uniform spacing through mandatory `period` in milliseconds.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 SampledData could not natively express per-sample offsets or irregular sampling intervals.

newState.summary: R6 adds optional `offsets` as a space-separated series of decimal offsets, mutually exclusive with `interval`.

constraints.human: A SampledData SHALL have either an interval and offsets but not both

semanticText.short: Offsets, typically in time, at which data values were taken
semanticText.definition: A series of increasing decimal values separated by a single space (character u20), which represent the offset from the logical start point. Offset values may be negative. The units in which the offsets are expressed are found in intervalUnit.  The absolute point at which the measurements begin SHALL be conveyed outside the scope of this datatype, e.g. Observation.effectiveDateTime for a timing offset.
semanticText.comment: If offsets is present, the number of data points must be equal to the number of offsets multipled by the dimensions.

newState.narrativeMd: `offsets` allows R6 data to express irregular sample positions in `intervalUnit` units.

facts.newValue: R6 requires exactly one of interval or offsets

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: `offsets` is a new R6 timing representation rather than a rename of any R4 element.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This does not make existing R4 instances invalid by itself, but it creates valid R6 content with no base R4 equivalent. A converter can only map `offsets` to R4 `period` when the offsets are uniformly spaced and can be expressed in milliseconds. Otherwise, dropping offsets changes the timing of the data.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Irregular sampling offsets may be clinically or analytically meaningful; collapsing them to a single period can distort the series.

justification.inferredGoal: Support irregularly sampled series without forcing a lossy uniform-period representation.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable: `offsets` is optional additive R6 content and does not make R4-valid SampledData instances invalid in R6 by itself.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The inferred goal of representing irregular sampling is reasonable and addresses a capability R4's single uniform `period` could not natively express. Since the element is an optional R6 addition, the compatibility issue is valid R6 content that cannot be faithfully exported to base R4, not preservation of R4-valid instances.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: No backward-compatible alternative is needed for R4-to-R6 instance preservation because old R4 instances do not contain `offsets`. R6 could have represented irregular offsets only through an extension, which would ease some R4 round-tripping, but that would make the feature less discoverable, less consistently validated, and less interoperable in base R6. Extension or sidecar preservation is a down-conversion mitigation, not a less-breaking base R6 design for this finding.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: R6-to-R4 conversion may need extensions or rejection for irregular data, but that is reverse-direction loss handling rather than an R4-to-R6 base-design alternative.

evidence.detail: R4 provides a single mandatory uniform period, with no offsets element.
R6 defines `offsets` as a string of increasing decimal offsets and states that the units come from `intervalUnit`.
evidence.quote: A series of increasing decimal values separated by a single space

examples.examplesMd: The offsets `0 4 9` are not uniformly spaced, so there is no single R4 `period` value that preserves all sample positions.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 adds `offsets` for irregular sample positions. This is a meaningful new capability, but it is not backward representable in base R4, which only understands a single uniform `period`.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R6 instance with `offsets` and no `interval` can validate in R6 under `sdd-1`. The same content is invalid as R4 because `offsets` and `intervalUnit` are unknown and R4 requires `period`. Even if a converter emits a period, the result is only valid and faithful when the offsets form a uniform sequence.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: For R6-to-R4, detect `offsets`. If offsets are uniformly spaced, convert the spacing to milliseconds and populate `period`; otherwise use an extension, preserve the original R6 payload, or reject with a clear lossiness error. Test irregular, negative, and multi-dimensional cases because the R6 comment ties point counts to offsets multiplied by dimensions.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A core element was likely needed to standardize irregular sampling. A standard extension would have been more backward compatible with R4 but less discoverable and less enforceable in base R6 validation.

freshReview.narrativeMd: `SampledData.offsets` is optional R6 support for irregularly spaced samples. It does not make an old R4 instance invalid by itself because old instances never had this element, but it creates valid R6 SampledData that base R4 cannot faithfully represent when offsets are non-uniform, negative, or otherwise not reducible to a single period. A down-converter may have to reject the instance, use an extension, or collapse timing information. As a new base capability for data R4 could not model, a core element is reasonable and an extension-only design would undercut interoperability.
keyEvidence: R4 SampledData has a single required `period` for uniform spacing and no `offsets` element.
R6 `SampledData.offsets` is 0..1 string containing increasing decimal offsets; its units come from `intervalUnit`.
R6 root invariant `sdd-1` makes `offsets` mutually exclusive with `interval`.
Observation.value[x] and Observation.component.value[x] expose SampledData in both releases.
freshReview.fmmEffect: Trial-use status reduces the expectation that R6 must preserve every R4-era limitation. The reverse-conversion loss is still meaningful because timing changes can alter interpretation, but it concerns new R6 expressiveness rather than preservation of old R4 content.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss: valid R6 irregular offsets have no base R4 representation except when they can be safely collapsed to a uniform millisecond period.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: No compelling less-breaking base R6 design exists for this specific optional capability. Keeping irregular timing only in an extension or sidecar could ease some R4 round-tripping, but it would fail the R6 goal of a discoverable, consistently validated base representation.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree with the existing High reverse-risk assessment and Not applicable alternative judgment; the fresh review emphasizes that this is not a forward R4-to-R6 instance break.

findings.title: R6 allows coded data tokens and adds `codeMap`, which R4 cannot round-trip

oldState.summary: R4 `data` was described as decimal values separated by spaces, with special values E, L, and U allowed.

semanticText.definition: A series of data points which are decimal values separated by a single space (character u20). The special values "E" (error), "L" (below detection limit) and "U" (above detection limit) can also be used in place of a decimal value.
semanticText.comment: Data may be missing if it is omitted for summarization purposes. In general, data is required for any actual use of a SampledData.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 semantics limited tokens to decimal values plus the three special non-numeric values.

newState.summary: R6 `data` allows decimal values or codes, and R6 adds optional `codeMap` canonical(ConceptMap) to define those codes.

semanticText.short: Decimal values with spaces, or "E" | "U" | "L", or another code
semanticText.definition: A series of data points which are decimal values or codes separated by a single space (character u20). The special codes "E" (error), "L" (below detection limit) and "U" (above detection limit) are also defined for used in place of decimal values.
semanticText.comment: The data may be missing if it is omitted for summarization purposes. In general, data is required for any actual use of a SampledData.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 keeps the same string type but broadens the token vocabulary and provides `codeMap` for code meanings.

facts.newValue: Decimal values with spaces, or "E" | "U" | "L", or another code

facts.oldValue: decimal values separated by a single space
facts.newValue: decimal values or codes separated by a single space

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: `data` is the same element path and type in both versions, but the allowed semantic content is broadened. `codeMap` is included in this finding because it supplies the meanings for the newly allowed coded tokens.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Old R4 numeric/E/L/U strings remain compatible at the base string level, so this is not an R4-to-R6 validation break. The risk is behavioral and reverse-conversion: R6 producers can send non-numeric tokens that R4 consumers or generated helper parsers may reject, misparse, or silently treat as invalid. R4 has no `codeMap` slot to preserve the code meanings.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: If coded data tokens represent clinically significant waveform annotations or device states, ignoring or misinterpreting them can change downstream interpretation.

justification.inferredGoal: Allow sampled data series to include coded observations or annotations beyond numeric values and the built-in E/L/U special codes.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable: R4 numeric and E/L/U `data` strings remain within the R6 semantic domain; the issue is R6-only coded tokens and `codeMap` round-tripping.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 goal of standardizing coded sampled-data tokens appears reasonable, and the local definitions show a semantic widening rather than an old-valid/new-invalid restriction. Existing R4 data strings remain structurally and semantically acceptable after the timing migration. The lack of concrete ConceptMaps or examples limits confidence in the exact use cases, so `Probably justified` is more appropriate than a stronger verdict.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: Under the calibration rule this is not an R4-to-R6 base break: the R6 datatype broadens what `data` may contain and adds optional `codeMap`. A design that kept `data` numeric-only and put coded tokens in a separate element, profile, or extension could reduce runtime surprise for parsers that assume decimals plus E/L/U, but it would not preserve any additional R4-valid instances. It would also fragment the compact token stream and make coded samples less uniform across R6 implementations.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: A separate coded-data field or extension would reduce surprise for numeric parsers, but it would split the series representation and is not needed to preserve R4-valid instances.

evidence.detail: R4 describes `data` as decimal values with only E, L, and U special values.
evidence.quote: decimal values separated by a single space

evidence.detail: R6 describes `data` as decimal values or codes and updates the short text to include another code.
evidence.quote: decimal values or codes separated by a single space

evidence.detail: R6 adds `codeMap` as 0..1 canonical targeting ConceptMap.
evidence.quote: Reference to ConceptMap that defines the codes used in the data.

examples.examplesMd: The example is illustrative. `N` and `PVC` are arbitrary code tokens whose meanings would need to come from the referenced ConceptMap; base R4 has no `codeMap` element and no base semantics for arbitrary data codes.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 changes `SampledData.data` from numeric values plus E/L/U to numeric values or codes, and adds `codeMap` to define those codes. Because the JSON type remains `string`, schema validation alone may not reveal the behavioral change; parsers that split the string and parse decimals are the likely failure point.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4-valid numeric data remains structurally acceptable after proper timing migration. Valid R6 coded data, however, is not cleanly representable in R4: the arbitrary code tokens exceed R4's semantic domain, and the `codeMap` canonical cannot be carried in the base R4 datatype. Strict R4 business validation or numeric parsing can fail at runtime even if a generic JSON parser accepts the string.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Inventory any code that parses `SampledData.data` tokens as decimals with only E/L/U exceptions. For R6, update parsers to detect and resolve coded tokens through `codeMap`. For R6-to-R4, either reject coded data, map codes to numeric or E/L/U values when clinically safe, or preserve the R6 representation in an extension or sidecar. Test mixed numeric/coded strings and reserved E/L/U behavior.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The broader semantics were not fully backward compatible with existing numeric assumptions. A separate coded-data field or extension would have made the change more explicit to parsers, but at the cost of splitting the compact series representation.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Human review should confirm intended coded-token grammar, reserved-code behavior, and whether any official ConceptMaps or examples constrain this feature more tightly than the local StructureDefinition text.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R6 keeps `SampledData.data` as a string but widens its token semantics from decimal values plus E/L/U to decimal values or codes, and adds optional `codeMap` to define code meanings. Existing R4 data strings remain within the R6 value domain, so this is not a structural old-valid/new-invalid break. The real risk is runtime and reverse compatibility: parsers that assume decimals/E/L/U may reject or misinterpret R6 coded tokens, and base R4 has no place to preserve `codeMap` meanings. The R6 goal is plausible, and without concrete cited production examples this looks like a proportionate R6-only expansion rather than a clear redesign candidate.
keyEvidence: R4 `SampledData.data` is a string of decimal values with special E, L, and U tokens.
R6 `SampledData.data` is still string but allows decimal values or codes, and `SampledData.codeMap` is 0..1 canonical targeting ConceptMap.
R6 `SampledData.codeMap` comment excludes redefining E/U/L and their lowercase forms.
Local package search found the element definitions but no concrete `codeMap` instances; a quick targeted web search did not establish cited production-use evidence.
freshReview.fmmEffect: Trial-use status and lack of quick production-use evidence soften the case for Revisit. The concern remains real if coded tokens represent clinically meaningful device states, but the supplied evidence supports a bounded compatibility burden rather than a disproportionate break.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: runtime/API/codegen and R6-to-R4 loss: decimal-token parsers may fail on valid R6 codes, and R4 cannot carry the `codeMap` canonical or coded-token semantics in the base datatype.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A separate coded-data element or profile/extension could reduce surprise for numeric parsers, but it would split the compact sample stream and would not preserve any additional R4-valid instances. There is no clearly better less-breaking base design without sacrificing the R6 goal.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree with the existing High impact and Not applicable alternative judgment; the fresh review agrees on runtime/reverse risk but gives less weight to impact because R4 data is widened, not invalidated, and production evidence was not found quickly.

findings.title: R6 adds error invariant requiring exactly one of `interval` or `offsets`

oldState.summary: R4 had no SampledData-local timing-choice invariant; regular timing was enforced by mandatory `period`.

constraints.human: All FHIR elements must have a @value or children

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 did not need a local interval/offset choice rule because it had only one timing representation, `period`.

newState.summary: R6 adds `sdd-1` as an error-level local invariant requiring exactly one of `interval` or `offsets`.

constraints.human: A SampledData SHALL have either an interval and offsets but not both

newState.narrativeMd: Although `interval` and `offsets` are each 0..1, the root invariant makes one and only one timing representation mandatory.

facts.newValue: exactly one of interval or offsets required

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The invariant is new and local to `SampledData`; inherited `ele-1` is not treated as a local change.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The invariant is an error-level validation rule. A correct R4-to-R6 transform that maps `period` to `interval` satisfies it, but a naive transform that drops `period` or a new R6 producer that sees `interval` as optional and omits both timing fields will fail validation. The apparent 0..1 cardinality of `interval` and `offsets` can mislead code generators unless invariants are enforced.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: A SampledData series without timing information is generally not interpretable; the invariant prevents that ambiguity in R6.

justification.inferredGoal: Preserve the requirement that SampledData have timing information while allowing either regular intervals or irregular offsets.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain `period` as a deprecated regular-timing alternative and make the base invariant require exactly one of retained `period`/regular interval or `offsets`.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: A base rule requiring interpretable timing is justified once R6 offers both regular intervals and irregular offsets; allowing neither or both would be unsafe and ambiguous. The avoidable part is narrower: the invariant could have acknowledged a retained R4 `period` path if the model had chosen to keep it. Because that alternative is entangled with duplicate or legacy timing representations, the current invariant is probably justified despite a partial less-breaking path.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design could express the timing choice as exactly one of a retained `period` regular-sampling representation and `offsets`, or exactly one of `period`, `interval`, and `offsets` if both regular fields were kept during transition. That would help raw R4 instances and older code, but it increases invariant complexity, requires precedence rules if two regular fields exist, and risks making deprecated representations permanent. A profile-only rule is not counted as a backward-compatible base alternative because it would leave base R6 instances with missing or conflicting timing valid.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: This would reduce migration failures, but it complicates the timing choice and may leave deprecated timing representations in use indefinitely.

evidence.detail: R4 root constraints contain inherited `ele-1` but no local `sdd-1` timing-choice invariant.
R6 root defines `sdd-1` with severity error and source SampledData.

examples.examplesMd: The example is R6-invalid because it has neither `interval` nor `offsets`, despite satisfying the raw 0..1 cardinalities. It is included to illustrate the invariant rather than an R6-to-R4 conversion case.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 adds the local invariant `sdd-1`. This is important because the new timing model cannot be understood from element cardinalities alone: both `interval` and `offsets` look optional, but validation requires exactly one.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: This can break R6 validation for migrated or newly created instances that omit both timing fields or populate both. The primary risk is not old R4 data that is correctly transformed; it is naive migration, code generation that ignores FHIRPath invariants, and validators that only check cardinality.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Migration tooling should implement `sdd-1` explicitly. Unit tests should include interval-only, offsets-only, neither, and both cases. UI and API models should present timing as a choice rather than two independent optional fields.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The invariant is justified by the added offsets capability. A less strict base model would be easier for producers but would allow uninterpretable or contradictory SampledData instances.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: The R6 root comment still says the data is not interpretable without `origin, period, and dimensions`, even though `period` no longer exists. The computable invariant appears authoritative, but the narrative wording should be reviewed.

freshReview.narrativeMd: `sdd-1` is an error-level invariant requiring exactly one of `interval` or `offsets`. R4 already required regular timing through `period`; the new rule preserves the requirement that SampledData have interpretable timing after R6 makes the two timing representations individually optional. It can reject naive migrations that drop `period` or new R6 instances that omit both or supply both timing choices, but that is guarding against uninterpretable or contradictory sample timing. The rule appears proportionate even though it is coupled to the period-to-interval redesign.
keyEvidence: R4 `SampledData.period` is 1..1, so R4 SampledData had a required timing amount.
R6 `SampledData.interval` and `SampledData.offsets` are each 0..1 and both list condition `sdd-1`.
R6 root constraint `sdd-1` has severity error and expression `interval.exists().not() xor offsets.exists().not()`.
R4 metadata checked: SampledData is trial-use.
freshReview.fmmEffect: Trial-use status softens the stability concern, and the invariant is primarily a computability/safety guard rather than an arbitrary new restriction. The coupling to the removed `period` path keeps it from being a pure no-op for migration.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: a raw R4 instance has `period` rather than `interval` or `offsets` and therefore fails the R6 timing-choice invariant; in practice this is tightly coupled to the period replacement. Validators and code generators must also account for the invariant despite 0..1 cardinalities.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A partial less-breaking design exists only if the old timing path were retained: the invariant could require exactly one of `period`, `interval`, or `offsets`, or one of retained `period` and `offsets`. That reduces migration failures but creates duplicate regular-timing representations, conflict rules, and a risk that deprecated timing paths remain permanent. Making the invariant warning-level or profile-only would allow missing or conflicting timing in base R6.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree with the existing Medium impact and Partial alternative judgment; the fresh review agrees this is potential and coupled, but treats the error invariant itself as a justified timing-safety rule.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: The R6 package contains `StructureDefinition-SampledData.json` with the same canonical URL, id, name, kind, type, and non-abstract flag. The baseDefinition shift is inherited/base scope and not counted as a local finding.

Continuing local elements `origin`, `factor`, `lowerLimit`, `upperLimit`, `dimensions`, and `data` retain their R4 cardinalities. Cardinality-relevant timing changes and the mandatory new `intervalUnit` are reported as findings.

Continuing local elements retain their types: `origin` remains SimpleQuantity, numeric modifiers remain decimal, `dimensions` remains positiveInt, and `data` remains string. New timing/codeMap types are reported in findings.
R4 SampledData had no local reference/canonical target. R6 adds `codeMap` targeting `ConceptMap`; that new target is covered in the coded-data finding.
No pre-existing local binding changed. R6 adds a required UCUM binding on the new `intervalUnit` element, reported as a finding.

No SampledData-local element is marked as a modifier in either version.

Continuing elements retain their summary status. The timing replacement preserves summary status for regular interval data (`period` in R4, `interval` and `intervalUnit` in R6); `offsets`, `codeMap`, and `data` are not summary elements in R6.
No SampledData-local slicing was found. Inherited `extension` slicing is out of scope.
